facts.statement: The genus Yuzhoupliosaurus was described by Zhang in 1985.
The genus name honors Yuzhou, the former name of Chongqing, the city where the first fossil was discovered.
facts.quote: The genus was named after Yuzhou (渝州), the previous name of Chongqing, a major city on the Yangtze River where the first fossil of Yuzhoupliosaurus was found.

facts.statement: Yuzhoupliosaurus lived in China during the Middle Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Yuzhoupliosaurus is an extinct genus of rhomaleosaurid plesiosaur found in rocks of the Middle Jurassic in China.

facts.statement: Researchers believe Yuzhoupliosaurus lived in freshwater environments.
facts.quote: It is believed this genus lived in fresh water.

facts.statement: The known fossil material consists of a lower jaw, eighteen vertebrae, pectoral girdle fragments, and parts of the right hindlimb.
facts.quote: The genus is known only from a lower jaw, eighteen vertebrae, fragments of a pectoral girdle and parts of the right hindlimb.

facts.statement: Paleontologists estimate Yuzhoupliosaurus was approximately four meters long.
facts.quote: Paleontologists believe Yuzhoupliosaurus to have been approximatively four meters long.

facts.statement: The lower jaws possessed five pairs of large teeth followed by 23 or 24 smaller teeth.
facts.quote: The lower jaws contain five pairs of large teeth and 23 or 24 smaller teeth.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae are described as being high and short.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebrae are considered "high and short".

facts.statement: Anterior cervical ribs are double-headed, whereas posterior cervical ribs are single-headed.
facts.quote: The anterior cervical ribs are double-headed while the posterior cervical ribs are single-headed.

facts.statement: The coracoids were elongated and the clavicles were well-developed.
facts.quote: The coracoids are elongated and the clavicles are well-developed.

facts.statement: Yuzhoupliosaurus is classified within the family Rhomaleosauridae.
The type species is Yuzhoupliosaurus chengjiangensis, described by Zhang in 1985.
Yuzhoupliosaurus lived between 174.7 and 161.5 million years ago, from the Aalenian to Callovian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aalenian to Callovian (174.7 to 161.5 million years ago)
